sections.name: What Actually Causes Hiccups
lines: Hic! Here's what's going on inside you when you hiccup.
Under your lungs is a dome shaped muscle called the diaphragm. It pulls air in every time you breathe.
Eat too fast, gulp a fizzy drink, or get excited, and it can suddenly spasm.
You suck in air, and a split second later, your vocal cords snap shut.
That slam is the hic sound.
Most hiccups stop within minutes. But one man, Charles Osborne, hiccupped for sixty-eight years.
Holding your breath, or slowly sipping cold water, can sometimes reset it.
